Cherry blossoms are among the most beautiful and admired flowers in the world. Known for their soft pink and white petals, these delicate blooms appear during the spring season and symbolize renewal, hope, beauty, and the short but meaningful nature of life. Cherry blossom trees, often called sakura in Japan, have become deeply connected to culture, art, poetry, and traditions across many countries. Every year, millions of people gather in parks, gardens, and streets to witness the brief but breathtaking blooming season that transforms landscapes into seas of pink and white. Cherry blossoms bloom for only a short period, usually lasting one to two weeks depending on weather conditions. This short life span is one reason they are so admired. Their beauty reminds people that life itself is temporary and precious. In Japanese culture, cherry blossoms represent the idea of living in the moment and appreciating beauty while it lasts. Festivals called hanami, meaning “flower viewing,” are held during the blooming season. Families and friends gather beneath the trees for picnics, music, laughter, and celebration while enjoying the falling petals drifting through the air like soft pink snow. The history of cherry blossoms dates back thousands of years. In ancient Japan, emperors and nobles admired the blossoms and wrote poetry inspired by them. Over time, the tradition spread throughout society and eventually became known around the world. Today, cherry blossom festivals are celebrated in many countries including the United States, South Korea, and China. One of the most famous celebrations outside Japan takes place in Washington, D.C., where thousands of cherry blossom trees bloom around the Tidal Basin each spring. These trees were gifted by Japan in 1912 as a symbol of friendship between nations.#fyp #fyp #fypシ゚viral #foryou #japan

Long lasting flowers and tons of colour? Grow these 🌸 If you’re a beginner gardener or someone planning next year’s garden, it’s so important to have long lasting colour in the borders and pots. These are my 8 favourite long lasting flowers that I’ve discovered after many years of growing 🌼 They all flower continuously for months and months even when most other plants in the garden have finished flowering, these plants just don’t stop! 🌸 Most are easy to care for apart from a bit of deadheading. The perennials come back every year (in the UK) and the annuals are easy to grow from seed 🌱 - Alstroemeria - Dahlias - Zinnias (my favourite is ‘Purple Prince’) - Salvia ‘mystic spires’ - Cosmos (my favourites are ‘sensation mix’ and ‘candy stripe’) - Rudbeckia (the longest lasting flowers are ‘Marmalade’) - Erigeron karvinskianus (Mexican fleabane) - Geranium Rozanne  #gardening #flowers #summer

Tulips are among the most beloved spring flowers, known for their bright colors and elegant shape. Originally from Central Asia, they became widely popular in the Netherlands during the 17th century, a period known as "Tulip Mania." Today, tulips symbolize perfect love, rebirth, and the arrival of spring. They come in nearly every color except true blue, and each color carries its own meaning — red for true love, yellow for cheerful thoughts, and purple for royalty.
